title: Resolve Bermuda territory tier and reusable boundary evidence

body:
2026-10-05: Bounded source-restoration and hierarchy follow-up from #427. Exact affected Atlas subject is `atlas:territory:BMU`; current parent is `framework:province:bermuda:9b939083e51d`.

The current Atlas aggregation records eleven Natural Earth source-member IDs/aliases: City of Hamilton, City of Saint George, Devonshire, Hamilton, Paget, Pembroke, Saint George’s, Sandys, Smith’s, Southampton and Warwick. Bermuda Government’s official 2016 Census Parish Profiles page lists nine named parish profiles. Current UK government guidance identifies Bermuda as a British Overseas Territory, but that fact does not certify its Atlas parent, internal administrative tier, coastal limits or historical political attributes. Natural Earth 10m is generalized and its retained geometry differs from the current Atlas aggregate; no legal-boundary conclusion follows.

A direct metadata-only lead was identified at the Bermuda Department of Land Surveys ArcGIS basemap service. Its layer metadata describes determined parish boundaries from the 2003 Topographic Map Database and 2003 coastline. The service credits the Department of Land Surveys & Registration and converter Kevin Mayall/Locus Ltd.; no reuse license was established. Only service/layer metadata was fetched and retained in #427, with exact hashes; no feature query, tile, or geometry download was made. This is historical source lineage, not a current reusable-boundary finding.

Research objective: obtain from Bermuda's Department of Land Surveys/National Mapping Office an authoritative, current, reusable whole-territory and internal-unit source, or a durable explicit restoration instruction if unavailable; reconcile whether the 2003 parish layer remains appropriate and its reuse terms; establish completeness (including offshore/island components), source roles, and whether the two city identities should be modeled separately from nine parish units; assess whether the coextensive Atlas province parent is only a framework grouping or has a sourced administrative meaning. Preserve `atlas:territory:BMU`, all historical identities and facts unless an authoritative source warrants a sourced correction proposal. No core changes, imports, sovereignty inference from Natural Earth, or reuse/export of restricted geometry.

Rejected candidate: a different surfaced ArcGIS `ParishBoundaries` listing was not accepted. Its live service extent is in Barbados, its item owner is `CarissChoong`, and its license text cites Barbados copyright despite Bermuda-like descriptive text. Only item/service/layer metadata was retained in #427's packet; no geometry was queried. A separate Esri/Michael Bauer Research Bermuda boundary item states its data may not be exported; its geometry was not accessed. The official Bermuda 1991 census-map URL returned 404 in the recorded retrieval attempt; use the official restoration links and citations in #427's packet, and verify contemporary reuse terms before retaining any replacement document/data.

Source references: Government of Bermuda [2016 Census Parish Profiles](https://www.gov.bm/articles/2016-population-and-housing-census-parish-profiles), [2016 Census report](https://www.gov.bm/articles/2016-population-and-housing-census-report), the 2003 Land Surveys service (`https://tiles.arcgis.com/tiles/YFNj7IqppWGZsn5o/arcgis/rest/services/basemap_2012/MapServer`), and current UK government [Bermuda status/travel reference](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/bermuda). Exact #427 receipts and hashes are in `sources/bermuda-official/` and `source/access-attempts.json` of its owned packet. This source research issue is blocked until the #427 evidence packet is merged and the required authoritative reusable evidence or restoration route is identified.
